central_answer: CURRENT RAWLSING VALIDATES A CALLER-SUPPLIED SOURCE SET. IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE, DERIVE, OR PERFORM SOURCE SELECTION FOR A SERVICE REQUEST.

allowed_dispositions_considered.rejected_because: No current owner exists. The concept occurs zero times in rawlsing_next and zero times in any adopted Field Forge/OBL authority.

There is nothing to split. The RELATION half is conserved; the APPLICABILITY half is absent at every grain, so no same-grain split exists and no composition can be proved to reproduce the historical function.

This was the closest alternative. It was rejected on a precise distinction: partial coverage requires the applicability DECISION to be taken somewhere with only the derivation missing. It is taken nowhere. The sole overlap is a caller-DECLARABLE state vocabulary (SOURCE_NOT_APPLICABLE / NOT_APPLICABLE), and a shared word is not a shared function.

allowed_dispositions_considered.why: No applicability object, no applicability relation kind, no service-scoped resolver, no selection-reason record, and no service parameter on any current input surface. The authority FORM itself is absent and must be authored before it can be implemented. The gap is bounded: it needs a new authority form at a grain the DAG already has a pattern for, not new architecture.

allowed_dispositions_considered.rejected_because: No conflict. D12G and D15 agree, current law does not contradict them, and pre553_source_relations.py preserves the D15 separation of applicability from relation rather than absorbing it.

B_refuse_inadmissible_sources.what_it_can_do: refuse a SUPPLIED universe that does not resolve to exactly one sealed release, that lacks positive exact authority, or whose proposed relation kind is not positively authorised
B_refuse_inadmissible_sources.what_it_cannot_do: determine that a source should never have been supplied; inapplicability is declared by the caller, not derived

C_choose_among_multiple_admissible.note: the query accepts a SET and emits per-source facts; there is no selector, ranker or preference order

D_compose_under_exact_authority.owner: pre553_empirical_query.py AUTHORIZED_COMPOSITE + pre553_source_relations.py I07 composite guard
D_compose_under_exact_authority.note: AUTHORIZED_COMPOSITE is a SEPARATE branch from SOURCE_INDEXED_MULTI_UNIVERSE per HQ203 recalibration; this audit does not conflate them

E_preserve_why_each_source_was_selected.note: execution receipts record what was run, not why a source was admitted; no selection occurred, so no rationale exists to record

F_distinguish_no_applicable_source_from_.owner: typed states in pre553_source_relations.py and pre553_empirical_objects.py, with FORBIDDEN_BACKFILL_TARGET_STATES
F_distinguish_no_applicable_source_from_.what_exists: SOURCE_NOT_APPLICABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE, NONCOMPARABLE, UNAVAILABLE, OBSERVED_ZERO, ZERO_SUPPORT, DECLARED_NONE are real typed states and backfill into them is structurally forbidden
F_distinguish_no_applicable_source_from_.what_is_missing: nothing COMPUTES 'no applicable source' from the request; a caller may declare it, and the declaration is respected and protected, but never derived

explicit_statement: SELECTION IS CALLER-SUPPLIED TODAY. The current system validates the caller's set; it does not author it. Validation has not been equated with selection anywhere in this audit.
superseded_material_not_imported: Per HQ203, no HQ201 F6/F7 ontology claim is imported here, and the HQ201 SOURCE_INDEXED_MULTI_UNIVERSE / AUTHORIZED_COMPOSITE mode conflation is explicitly not repeated.
recommended_next_step_for_HQ: Accept that H-C is an authority-FORM gap, not an implementation gap.
Commission a bounded per-service source applicability contract (five required elements listed in 05), authored as authority before any code.
Keep the applicability decision strictly upstream of and non-substitutable by the relation powers, per D12G and the D15 ledger separation.

Decide whether an applicability authority failure is a typed nonapplicability (recoverable, per-source) or a service refusal (terminal). The historical ledger supports the former; current law has no instance to inherit it from.
